title: Reliance to Weigh Debenture Fundraise as It Declares Q2 Earnings on October 30
excerpt: The board meets Friday to approve results for the quarter ended September 30 and consider raising funds through listed non-convertible debentures on a private placement basis — two days after Jio Platforms lists following its Rs 30,213 crore IPO.
body:
• Reliance Industries will announce Q2 FY27 results on Friday, October 30, for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.
  • The board will also consider raising funds through listed, secured or unsecured, redeemable non-convertible debentures on a private placement basis, in one or more tranches; no amount or terms have been disclosed.
  • The results land two days after Jio Platforms lists on the BSE and NSE, following a Rs 30,213 crore IPO that was subscribed 22.19 times at Rs 1,119 per share.
  • Baseline for Friday: in Q1 FY27, Reliance reported record core profit with consolidated revenue up 25.4% year on year to Rs 3.12 lakh crore.

Reliance Industries Limited will announce its financial results for the second quarter of FY27 on Friday, October 30, with its board also scheduled to consider a proposal to raise funds through non-convertible debentures, the company said in an exchange filing on Tuesday, reported by ANI.

What the Board Will Consider

The board of directors will meet on October 30 to consider and approve the standalone and consolidated unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026. It will also consider raising funds through the issuance of listed, secured or unsecured, redeemable non-convertible debentures on a private placement basis, in one or more tranches. The company has not disclosed the proposed fundraising amount or the terms of the issuance. Reliance said it will hold an analyst meeting after the board meeting to discuss its performance for the September quarter and the first half of FY27.

Two Days After the Jio Listing

The earnings announcement comes as the group's digital arm, Jio Platforms, prepares to list on the BSE and NSE on Wednesday, October 28, after its initial public offering. The Rs 30,213 crore IPO opened for subscription on October 21 and closed on October 23, with a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. The issue comprised a fresh issuance of up to 27 crore shares with no offer-for-sale component, and included reservations of up to Rs 2,500 crore for eligible Reliance shareholders and Rs 500 crore for eligible employees. The issue was subscribed 22.19 times overall, and the price was fixed at Rs 1,119, the upper end of the band.

The Bar From Q1

Investors will judge Friday's numbers against a strong June quarter. In Q1 FY27, Reliance reported record quarterly core profit and EBITDA, with consolidated revenue rising 25.4% year on year to Rs 3.12 lakh crore, powered by its oil-to-chemicals and telecom businesses, according to Upstox. The size and pricing of any debenture program the board approves — and management's commentary at the analyst meeting — will signal how the group plans to fund its next round of expansion now that Jio carries its own public valuation.

Debenture issues of this kind are a routine funding tool for Reliance, which taps the domestic bond market alongside bank lines to finance capital spending across energy, retail and telecom. Because the filing gives neither an amount nor a coupon, Friday's board outcome — not the agenda itself — will be the market signal: approval would confirm the group is pre-funding while Jio's listing proceeds are still being deployed, and the results call will be the first chance for analysts to test management on how the two balance sheets now fit together.
